text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.3% today to $141.22, driven by a sharp rise in oil prices following Saudi Arabia's closure of a major pipeline after a drone attack. U.S. crude spiked above $105 a barrel, and the gap between U.S. and world oil prices has widened to over $12 per barrel—a spread that typically benefits refiners and integrated producers like ConocoPhillips. The U.S. Energy Secretary suggested the closure will last only days, but analysts are warning that if the pipeline stays offline longer than five to seven days, prices could rally further as inventory cushions shrink.

This move fits into a broader pattern: oil prices have climbed steadily over the past two weeks as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East create supply uncertainty, with the Houthi strikes and Iranian diplomatic activity adding to the regional instability. ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, particularly when global oil sits meaningfully higher than U.S. oil—a sign of tight supply that rewards producers with access to global markets.
